Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 26-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Number Theory and Cryptography [IT_3130]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                     a. Compute the number of integers between 000 and 999 (inclusive) which satisfy                    (5)  
  n≡7(mod11),n≡3(mod13) ?  
  A)                b. Construct the Additive and multiplicative inverse modulo 8 Caley table.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                a. Apply the concept of Euclid's Algorithm to find the GCD of 385 and 792, and hence express (5)  
  it in the form of 385x + 792y.  
  b. Illustration CIA model.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Compute the remainder when 23 130 is divided by 25.                                                     (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Solve the following system of congruences using the Chinese remainder theorem. Show your steps (5)  
  and reduce your answer to an element in Z746130.  
  $$x = 2 mod 11,$$  
  $$x = 3 mod 14,$$  
  $$x = 4 mod 15,$$  
  $$x = 5 mod 17,$$  
  $$x = 6 mod 19.$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Let (R, +, *) be an algebraic structure that satisfies all the ring axioms except commutativity of      (5)  
  addition. Show that if R has a unity, then R is a ring.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           a. Using CRT, solve for x for the following                                                             (5)  
  x ≡ 2 (mod 3)  
  x ≡ 3 (mod 5)  
  x ≡ 2(mod 7)  
  b. Find all the primitive roots of 25.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

4)              Using this Playfair matrix                                                                              (5)  
  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Encrypt this message:  
  I only regret that I have but one life to give for my country.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Consider 0-based alphabet indexing. You are given a plain text "COMPUTE" which is supposed to           (5)  
  be converted as follows : (eachletter's index value + 12) mod 26 to form a new plain text. Encrypt  
  this new plain text with a 3 * 3 key matrix as shown below  
  
  
  Compute the ciphertext.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)              Suppose the DES F function mapped every 32-bit input R, regardless of the value of the input K, to; (5)  
  a. 32-bit string of zero  
  A)         b. R  
  Then  
  1. What function would DES then compute?  
  2. What would the decryption look like?  
  Justify your answer with illustration.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         You are given the following plaintext block (in hexadecimal)                                            (5)  
  $$P = [32, 43, F6, A8, 88, 5A, 30, 8D, 31, 31, 98, A2, E0, 37, 07, 34] and the 16-byte cipher key$$  
  $$K = [2B, 28, AB, 09, 7E, AE, F7, CF, 15, D2, 15, 4F, 16, A6, 88, 3C]$$  
  Perform the first round of AES encryption. (In mix columns multiply with the below matrix)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
